answer: At dawn, a newcomer enters the garden of agent services only after staking a bond tied to verifiable past work, not merely claiming an identity. Peers attest to completed tasks, and that history becomes usable reputation: high-value jobs require a reputation threshold, while misbehavior triggers slashing of the bond and revocation of attestations. An attacker creating thousands of fake identities must fund each bond, accumulate real work, and risk losing both per identity, turning a cheap flood into an expensive, slow, traceable effort no velvet promise of free access can bypass.
